column1: # Disputes settled by hand (PROTOCOL.md §2: no majority votes). When systems of one regime
# report different answer counts for a query, the item stays "disputed" in every reader
# until a line here gives the correct count and why; then systems with that count are
# undisputed and the others' rows count as wrong. Columns, tab-separated:

column5: SELECT ?s ?label over the one pattern ?s rdfs:label ?label returns one row per triple; olympics.nt (frozen, benches/datasets.toml) holds 137,026 distinct rdfs:label triples (grep | sort -u | wc -l, 3 Oct 2026). Virtuoso returns 42 more.

SELECT DISTINCT ?x ?y { ?x :knows ?y } with knows an owl:ReflexiveProperty (in OWL 2 QL): owl2bench-ql-1.nt (frozen, benches/datasets.toml) asserts 1,427 knows pairs, none of a term with itself, and uses 3,677 terms as individuals (class members, object property ends, data property subjects); under the Direct Semantics each knows itself: 1,427 + 3,677 = 5,104. NRESE's owl2-ql ruleset lacked reflexive properties until e17ec26. Applies to the owl2-ql regime; OWL 2 RL has no reflexive properties (5 Oct 2026).

SELECT ?x { ?x dbo:subdivision+ dbr:Bavaria }: a one-or-more path has set semantics (SPARQL 1.1 §9.3, ALP), one row per distinct ?x. dbpedia-core.nt (frozen, benches/datasets.toml) has 1,090,641 distinct dbo:subdivision triples; walking them backwards from dbr:Bavaria reaches 21 distinct subjects (grep + a breadth-first walk, 5 Oct 2026). NRESE, QLever, Oxigraph and Jena return 21; Virtuoso returns 25.
